workflows.title: Starting a new project
preconditions: Workspace and safety boundaries are known
steps: Research only decisions that affect the first slice
Write a short spec with at most three milestones
Scaffold and prove one end-to-end path
Add repository instructions only for non-obvious commands
workflows.prompt: We are starting [PROJECT]. First ask only questions whose answers materially change the architecture. Then propose three approaches from simplest to most extensible, with tradeoffs. After I choose, write a three-milestone spec. Do not implement yet.
checks: Build and tests run from documented commands
No secret or generated artifact is committed
workflows.recovery: Return to the smallest end-to-end slice and defer speculative components.

workflows.title: Understanding an unfamiliar repository
preconditions: Question or feature area is known
steps: Record uncertainties and likely change surface
workflows.prompt: Map [BEHAVIOR] through this repository. Cite files and symbols for every claim. Identify entry points, data flow, invariants, tests, commands, and uncertainties. Do not edit.
workflows.recovery: Narrow to one request path and verify each hop in code.

workflows.title: Planning a feature
steps: Name files, checks, and rollback points
workflows.prompt: Plan [FEATURE] after inspecting the relevant code. Preserve [INVARIANTS]. Compare options, recommend one, and split it into independently testable slices. Include files, tests, risks, and non-goals. Do not edit.
workflows.recovery: Rewrite each step as a demonstrable behavior.

workflows.title: Implementing a feature
steps: Run broad suite and manual acceptance
workflows.prompt: Implement only slice [N] of the approved plan. Follow nearby patterns, avoid unrelated refactors, run [FOCUSED_CHECKS], and stop with a diff summary and open questions.
workflows.recovery: Revert or isolate the current slice, restate constraints, and retry smaller.

workflows.title: Debugging
workflows.objective: Prove the root cause and retain a regression guard.
workflows.prompt: Investigate [SYMPTOM]. Do not edit until you have a reproduction and at least two falsifiable hypotheses. Cite logs/code for the leading cause, then propose the smallest fix and regression test.
workflows.recovery: Discard unsupported edits and restart from the nearest observable boundary.

workflows.title: Refactoring
workflows.prompt: Refactor [TARGET] to improve [MEASURE]. Preserve public behavior and avoid feature changes. First identify coverage gaps; then make small steps, running [CHECKS] after each.
workflows.recovery: Restore last green commit and split the structural move further.

workflows.title: Writing and running tests
workflows.objective: Build trustworthy feedback rather than decorative coverage.
steps: Choose the lowest useful test seam
Verify it fails for the right reason
Review test for vacuity and brittleness
workflows.prompt: Write a regression test for [BEHAVIOR]. First show why it fails on current code. Assert public outcomes, not implementation trivia. Then implement the smallest fix and run [SUITE].
workflows.recovery: Move the assertion closer to the observable contract.

workflows.title: Reviewing changes
workflows.objective: Find requirement, correctness, safety, and maintainability defects.
workflows.prompt: Review the current diff against [REQUIREMENT]. Prioritize correctness, security, data loss, concurrency, and missing tests. Cite files/lines and explain reproduction. Do not edit.
workflows.recovery: Use a fresh session and ask it to falsify the implementation.

workflows.title: Preparing a pull request
workflows.objective: Create a reviewable, evidence-backed draft PR.
workflows.prompt: Prepare a draft PR for [CHANGE]. First inspect the full branch diff. Draft a concise summary, behavioral changes, test evidence, risks, and rollout notes. Do not push until I approve.
workflows.recovery: Keep the PR draft, amend commits and description, rerun checks.

workflows.title: Handling a large codebase
workflows.objective: Find relevant context without flooding the main session.
steps: Start from symbols and execution boundaries
Use targeted search before broad reads
Delegate independent maps to read-only subagents
workflows.prompt: For [QUESTION], use targeted search and delegate at most [N] independent read-only investigations. Return one evidence map with paths, symbols, uncertainties, and the minimal files needed next.
checks: Main context receives summaries, not raw dumps
workflows.recovery: Collapse to one vertical path and one owner.

workflows.title: Managing context
workflows.objective: Preserve relevant evidence while removing noise.
workflows.prompt: Create a handoff for a fresh session: goal, constraints, decisions and rationale, changed files, commands/results, failed approaches, open risks, and exact next action. Verify it against the repository.
workflows.recovery: Reconstruct from Git, test output, and local session history.

workflows.title: Recovering from a poor trajectory
workflows.objective: Stop compounding mistakes and restart with better evidence.
steps: Press Esc and prevent further actions
Inspect status/diff and external side effects
Rewind, undo, or revert exact changes
workflows.prompt: Stop. The trajectory violates [CONSTRAINT]. Inspect current status and explain exactly what changed and what external actions occurred. Propose the safest targeted recovery; do not execute it until reviewed.
workflows.recovery: Use Git plus manual inspection; checkpoints do not cover every Bash/external change.

workflows.title: Using multiple agents or parallel work
steps: Choose subagents for reads and worktrees for writes
Integrate one branch at a time
workflows.prompt: Decompose [TASK] into independent work. Parallelize only non-overlapping scopes; assign each agent an evidence/output contract. Keep integration and shared-file decisions with the lead.
workflows.recovery: Pause writers, reconcile a single baseline, then reassign narrower scopes.

workflows.title: Safely automating repeated work
workflows.objective: Encode a proven workflow with bounded authority.
steps: Limit paths, tools, time, and network
workflows.prompt: Design a non-interactive automation for [WORKFLOW]. Begin read-only. Specify inputs, output schema, tools, timeouts, forbidden actions, validation, human gates, and rollback. Do not implement until threat-modeled.
workflows.recovery: Disable trigger, preserve logs, restore last known output, return to manual loop.

workflows.title: Security review
workflows.prompt: Review [SCOPE] as a security engineer. Map trust boundaries, then inspect injection, authn/authz, secrets, unsafe deserialization, data exposure, and command execution. Cite code and provide a realistic exploit path; do not invent findings.
workflows.recovery: Use a fresh read-only reviewer and validate high-severity findings manually.

prompts.title: Evidence map
prompts.text: Map [BEHAVIOR] through this repository. Cite paths and symbols; identify entry points, data flow, invariants, tests, commands, and uncertainties. Do not edit.

prompts.title: Option-first plan
prompts.text: For [OUTCOME], inspect current code, compare three options from simplest first, recommend one, and produce verified behavioral slices with files, tests, risks, and non-goals. Do not edit.

prompts.title: One slice
prompts.text: Implement only [SLICE]. Preserve [INVARIANTS], follow adjacent patterns, avoid unrelated refactors, run [CHECKS], and report the diff plus residual risks.

prompts.title: Falsifiable diagnosis
prompts.text: Reproduce [SYMPTOM]. Before editing, give competing hypotheses and the evidence that would distinguish them. Prove the leading cause, add a regression test, then make the smallest fix.

prompts.title: Behavior-preserving refactor
prompts.text: Refactor [TARGET] to improve [MEASURE] while preserving [CONTRACT]. Add characterization coverage if needed; make small steps and run [CHECKS] after each.

prompts.title: Meaningful regression
prompts.text: Write a regression test for [BEHAVIOR]. Demonstrate it fails for the correct reason before the fix. Assert public outcomes and review the test for vacuity and brittleness.

prompts.title: Decision record
prompts.text: Evaluate [DECISION] under [CONSTRAINTS]. Compare the simplest viable options, cite repository evidence, list reversibility and migration cost, and write a short ADR recommendation.

prompts.title: Fresh-context review
prompts.text: Review the diff against [REQUIREMENT]. Prioritize correctness, security, data loss, concurrency, and missing tests. Cite exact evidence and reproduction; omit unsupported speculation.

prompts.title: Docs from behavior
prompts.text: Update documentation for [CHANGE] using verified commands and current behavior. Identify stale claims, add one working example, and do not claim checks that were not run.

prompts.title: Threat-boundary review
prompts.text: Map trust boundaries for [SCOPE], then inspect untrusted input, authn/authz, secrets, injection, data exposure, and command execution. Rank only evidenced findings by exploitability.

prompts.title: Measure before optimize
prompts.text: Investigate [PERFORMANCE_SYMPTOM]. Establish a reproducible baseline and profile before editing. Compare hypotheses, change one variable, and report before/after data with uncertainty.

prompts.title: Durable handoff
prompts.text: Write a handoff containing goal, constraints, decisions, changed files, commands/results, failed approaches, open risks, and exact next action. Verify it against repository state.

prompts.title: Trajectory reset
prompts.text: Stop. [CONSTRAINT] was violated. Inspect status and external effects, explain exactly what happened, and propose a targeted recovery that preserves unrelated work. Do not execute yet.

prompts.title: Evidence-backed draft PR
prompts.text: Inspect the complete branch diff for [CHANGE]. Draft summary, behavioral changes, verification actually run, risks, and rollout. Identify unrelated edits. Do not push until approved.

decisions.question: Should I ask for a plan first?
rules: If the change crosses components, affects data/contracts, or the repo is unfamiliar → plan first.
If it is localized, reversible, and directly testable → edit with a brief mini-plan.

decisions.question: Should I split this task?
rules: If one success check cannot cover it or failures are hard to localize → split by behavior.
If slices would require constant shared-state coordination → keep one owner.

decisions.question: Should I start a fresh session?
rules: New topic, repeated forgotten constraints, or two failed corrections → write a handoff and start fresh.
Same coherent investigation with useful evidence → continue or compact selectively.

decisions.question: Should I use a subagent?
rules: Independent, read-heavy, specialist, or noisy task with a concise output → use one.
Shared files, rapid back-and-forth, or integration decisions → keep central.

decisions.question: Should I update CLAUDE.md?
rules: Stable non-obvious rule repeated across tasks → add concise guidance at the narrowest scope.
Temporary state, obvious practice, or a one-off correction → do not add.

decisions.question: Should I use MCP?
rules: Needed external capability lacks a good CLI/API path and has clear permissions → consider MCP.
A direct CLI works or integration cost exceeds repeated value → skip it.

decisions.question: Should I write tests first?
rules: Bug, stable behavioral contract, or risky refactor → usually write regression/characterization first.
Exploratory spike with unknown shape → prototype, then discard or backfill before production.

decisions.question: Should I refactor before the feature?
rules: A small prerequisite unlocks a test seam and can be behavior-preserving → separate refactor first.
Broad cleanup is merely attractive → ship the smallest feature slice without it.

decisions.question: Should I permit automatic command execution?
rules: Exact, reversible, local command in a constrained environment → narrowly allowlist.
Push, deploy, deletion, credentials, unknown network, or broad path → retain approval or isolate.

decisions.question: Is the agent stuck or merely exploring?
rules: New evidence and narrowing hypotheses → exploring; set a checkpoint.
Repeating tools, explanations, or failed edits without new evidence → stop, summarize, and reset.

antiPatterns.title: The vague vibe prompt
antiPatterns.symptoms: Large surprising diff and subjective completion claims.
antiPatterns.root: No outcome, constraints, or evidence target.

antiPatterns.title: One-shotting a large feature
antiPatterns.symptoms: Many files change before anything runs.

antiPatterns.title: Context hoarding
antiPatterns.root: Unrelated history and failed paths remain active.

antiPatterns.title: Confidence as verification
antiPatterns.symptoms: The agent says it double-checked but supplies no evidence.
antiPatterns.why: Plausibility is correlated with the same mistake.
antiPatterns.correction: Run a reproduction, test, typecheck, diff, or independent review.

antiPatterns.title: The encyclopedia CLAUDE.md
antiPatterns.symptoms: Rules are ignored and every session starts bloated.
antiPatterns.root: Stable constraints mixed with obvious or stale material.

antiPatterns.title: Permission fatigue
antiPatterns.symptoms: Every approval is clicked without reading.
antiPatterns.correction: Allowlist exact safe commands and sandbox risky work.
antiPatterns.prevention: Audit approvals and keep irreversible actions manual.

antiPatterns.title: Parallel collision
antiPatterns.symptoms: Agents overwrite or repeatedly rebase each other.
antiPatterns.correction: Use worktrees and one integration owner.

antiPatterns.title: Refactor smuggling
antiPatterns.root: Aesthetic improvement is bundled with behavior.

antiPatterns.title: Plugin maximalism
antiPatterns.symptoms: High context cost, unclear triggers, broad permissions.
antiPatterns.root: Extensions installed without a measured need.
antiPatterns.correction: Remove unused integrations; choose the smallest mechanism.

antiPatterns.title: Automating an unproven loop
antiPatterns.root: Workflow failure modes were never characterized.
antiPatterns.correction: Return to a supervised, read-only loop.
antiPatterns.prevention: Automate only after reliable manual repetitions.
